acceptedFindings.title: Manuscript omits all key statistical results
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The Abstract and Results sections mention only sample size, ignoring the estimated treatment effect, p-value, and confidence interval. Readers cannot evaluate the study's primary finding.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Update the manuscript to include the Welch t-test results: means, mean difference, Cohen's d, test statistic, p-value, and confidence interval.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: manuscript.md abstract and results lack any numeric estimates.

acceptedFindings.title: Manuscript contradicts available evidence
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The Limitations section claims 'No estimate-like records were available for p-value/effect-size checks,' but the stats-run.json clearly contains an estimates array with p-value and effect size. This inconsistency undermines trust in the entire report.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Reconcile the manuscript with the actual run output; remove the false statement.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: stats-run.json contains an 'estimates' key with p_value and cohen_d; manuscript.md says the opposite.

acceptedFindings.title: Analysis is unbound and purely exploratory
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The run's resultPosture is 'exploratory_standard_table' and cannot support paper-ready conclusions. Presenting it as a study answer is misleading and a claim-safety risk.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Bind the run to a preregistered method-selection and AnalysisSpec, or explicitly downgrade the report to exploratory data analysis with no confirmatory claims.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: stats-run.json binding.status is 'unbound', resultPosture.label is 'Exploratory standard-table result'.

acceptedFindings.title: Manuscript claims no estimate records, but they exist in artifacts
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Indicates manuscript not updated to reflect analysis output; undermines credibility.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Update the limitations section to accurately reflect that estimate records are available and report key results like mean difference, p-value, and effect size.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check that the limitations section no longer says 'No estimate-like records were available...'

acceptedFindings.title: No specific research question or clinical context stated
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without a clear question, the analysis cannot be evaluated for appropriateness or clinical utility.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Explicitly state the research question (PICO elements) in the Introduction and link it to the analysis.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Presence of a clearly stated question in the manuscript.

acceptedFindings.title: Observational comparison lacks any confounding adjustment or balance assessment
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The observed difference could be due to confounders; a simple t-test is insufficient for causal inference or even association without covariate control.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Either incorporate covariates in a regression model or clearly state that the analysis is purely descriptive and cannot distinguish confounding. Provide baseline characteristics table.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Existence of a table of baseline characteristics by group and a causal diagram or covariate adjustment plan.

acceptedFindings.title: Cohort construction, eligibility criteria, and variable definitions are missing
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Reproducibility and interpretation require knowing how the sample was derived and what the variables represent.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Describe data source, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and operational definitions of treatment and outcome (e.g., treatment type, outcome measurement).
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Presence of a detailed cohort flow diagram and variable dictionary.

acceptedFindings.title: Complete-case analysis without missing data investigation
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Only 240 complete cases were used, but the original sample size, missingness proportion, and missing-data mechanism are not reported. Non-random missingness could bias the estimate.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report the number of excluded records, reasons for missingness, and a sensitivity analysis (e.g., pattern-mixture, multiple imputation).

acceptedFindings.title: No normality or outlier diagnostics reported
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The Welch t-test assumes approximate normality, especially with small groups. The only diagnostic is Levene's test for equal variance, which is not required. Without Q-Q plots or Shapiro-Wilk results, the validity of the p-value is uncertain.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide distribution plots (histograms, Q-Q) per group and a formal normality test; discuss robustness.

acceptedFindings.title: Cohort definition and variable metadata missing
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: No information on how treatment groups were defined, what outcome_cont measures, or the eligibility criteria is provided. Interpretation and replication are impossible.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add a detailed cohort flowchart, variable definitions, and source data description.

acceptedFindings.title: Manuscript does not clearly convey the exploratory and unbound nature of the analysis
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Readers may overinterpret the results; the 'result posture' explicitly warns against inference.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add a prominent statement that this is an exploratory analysis not governed by a pre-specified protocol or analysis plan, and that claims are local.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Presence of the phrase 'exploratory' and 'unbound' in the limitations or abstract.

acceptedFindings.title: Complete-case analysis with no missing data exploration
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: If missingness is non-random, the complete-case analysis may be biased; the manuscript acknowledges the risk but provides no diagnostics.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report the proportion of missing data, compare characteristics of complete vs. incomplete cases, and consider sensitivity analysis or multiple imputation.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Presence of a missing data analysis section or justification for complete-case.

acceptedFindings.title: No descriptive statistics beyond group means
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Standard deviations, ranges, and quantiles are essential to assess data quality, effect-size interpretation, and potential floor/ceiling effects. Their absence prevents full evaluation.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Include a table of descriptive statistics (N, mean, SD, median, min, max) for each group.

acceptedFindings.title: Figure QA artifact appears truncated, and figure content not described in text
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The boxplot is not referenced or interpreted in the manuscript; its quality cannot be fully assessed.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Ensure the figure QA is complete and the manuscript includes a reference to the figure, with interpretation.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Figure referenced in manuscript and QA complete.

acceptedFindings.title: No comparison to existing literature or clinical significance
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without context, the effect size cannot be interpreted (e.g., is d=0.87 meaningful?).
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Discuss the observed effect relative to known minimal clinically important differences or prior studies.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Presence of a discussion paragraph linking results to literature.

finding.title: No literature context or prior effect estimates
finding.whyItMatters: For interpretability, the observed Cohen's d needs benchmarking against similar studies. Omission limits the reader's ability to assess external consistency or plausibility.
finding.actionableFix: Briefly cite comparable studies or known effect sizes for this outcome–treatment pair.

rejectedFindings.reason: Low-severity single-reviewer finding kept as advisory but not accepted for automatic repair.

reviewAdjudication.nextAction: Route back to protocol with review-response decisions.
